analysis_plan.control_comparison: governed versus random_walk on held-out delta, at identical budget and identical mutation operators. Only the selection differs.
analysis_plan.null_handling: Recorded as measured. A task the mutator cannot reach is reported as unreached, and no operator is added afterwards to reach it.
analysis_plan.overfitting: A development delta exceeding the held-out delta is reported as overfitting, not smoothed over.
analysis_plan.primary: Per task per arm: mean held-out delta across seeds, and the development delta alongside it so overfitting is visible.

arms.governed: mutate from the incumbent; promote on development improvement
arms.null_only: propose semantic no-ops and keep the best by development score. End-to-end phantom-gain check; must be exactly zero.
arms.random_walk: mutate identically but never select; report the final candidate. Separates search from mutation.

capability_claim_boundary: Any positive result is a claim about a generic mutation search on four small Python tasks. It is NOT evidence of model self-improvement, of a recursive effect, or of anything about the scaffold improving itself. The proposer is an AST mutator with no model in the loop.
claim_boundary: A governed generic-mutation search on four small deterministic Python tasks, scored on held-out cases. Not evidence of model self-improvement or of a recursive effect.

instrument.primary_metric: held-out normalised delta against the starting solution

predictions.basis: E69 measured best-of-k phantom gain at exactly zero. This checks the property end to end through the search loop rather than in isolation.
predictions.statement: null_only yields exactly 0.0 held-out delta on every task and every seed.

predictions.basis: collatz_steps is reachable by a single constant mutation.
predictions.statement: governed achieves a strictly positive mean held-out delta on at least one task.

predictions.basis: Its fix is returning -1 instead of 0 for non-positive n, which the constant operator produces directly.
predictions.statement: collatz_steps is the task governed search improves most.

predictions.basis: digit_sum_graded and count_one_bits need a structural insertion the operators cannot generate. Recorded in advance so an unreached task is not later presented as a surprise.
predictions.statement: At least one task shows a mean held-out delta of 0.0 under governed search.

predictions.basis: The two arms share operators, budget and seeds; only selection differs. If selection buys nothing, the governed loop is doing no work.
predictions.statement: governed's mean held-out delta exceeds random_walk's, pooled across tasks.

promotion_rule: A candidate is promoted only if it strictly improves the incumbent's development score. Ties are not promoted, so a no-op can never displace an incumbent.
proposer: recursive_lab.program_mutation: generic AST edits to constants, comparisons, arithmetic operators, signs and branch order. No operator encodes a task fix.
question: On an admissible deterministic substrate, does a governed mutation search produce held-out correctness improvements that a matched-budget unselected control does not?

split.method: Stratified alternation: cases the starting solution fails are dealt alternately to development and held-out, and likewise the cases it passes. Both halves are therefore guaranteed to contain fixable cases and regression-detecting cases.
